Your ≈€1,180/mo of free cash after fixed costs is real headroom. The deposit needs ≈€830/mo to land by June 2028 — that's ≈35% of take-home, and your own estimate says doable. The gap isn't ambition, it's the ≈€780/mo of drift: free cash that isn't going to eating out, isn't going to saving, and right now has no name.

The move: set up a standing transfer of ≈€300/mo on payday. Sized at roughly half the drift, it won't bite. At that pace the deposit lands in ≈37 months instead of ≈80. That's the security you said matters — moved from a target to a timeline.

You called the drift (≈€780/mo) unsure. That's the right call. A real month says whether it's spending you'd own, or just money that disappeared — and that answer changes everything about what's actually available.

Two things checking adds: it swaps every ≈ for a real number, so you can see estimate versus reality side by side. And the habits half of the picture is still completely empty — timing, patterns, what's recurring — because estimates can't see it, and only real transactions can.

Right now, I know you about 56%. Checking a real month is what takes that past 70%.

[CTA:start_statement_check]Check my numbers[/CTA]

— C.
